Two religious men walked past him. The one who stopped was the one nobody expected. 🩹 Luke 10

A lawyer asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbour?” (Luke 10:29). Jesus answered with a story: a priest and a Levite passed by on the other side, but a Samaritan “had compassion on him” and took care of him. Then Jesus said: “Go, and do thou likewise” (Luke 10:37).

Who's someone you've been tempted to walk past? Pray for them today 👇

They laughed at his wall. He finished it in 52 days. 🧱 Nehemiah 1-6

When Nehemiah heard Jerusalem's wall was broken down, he “sat down and wept” (Nehemiah 1:4), fasted and prayed. Mocked and threatened, the builders worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other. His answer to every distraction: “I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down” (Nehemiah 6:3).

What's the “great work” God has you building right now? 👇

The whole city asked one question: Who is this? 🌿 Matthew 21

Jesus rode into Jerusalem just as the prophet said: “Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek” (Matthew 21:5). The crowds spread their garments and branches in the way and cried, “Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord” (Matthew 21:9). Then in the temple He overthrew the tables and healed the blind and the lame.

How would you answer “Who is this?” in one word? 👇

Just wash seven times in a river? He almost walked away. 🌊 2 Kings 5

Naaman was a mighty captain, “but he was a leper” (2 Kings 5:1). Elisha didn't even come out, he just sent word: “Go and wash in Jordan seven times.” Naaman left in a rage, until his servants asked, “if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it?” (2 Kings 5:13). He obeyed, and “his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean” (2 Kings 5:14).

What small step of obedience is God asking of you this week? 👇
